a: Call +91 9832093139 or email cacslalitgupta@gmail.com. Please check the contact page for current hours before visiting.

q: How quickly will you respond to my enquiry?
a: We aim to respond within one working day. Urgent notices are prioritised.

q: Why choose a chartered accountant instead of a general tax filer?
a: A chartered accountant is a regulated professional who can certify, audit and represent you before authorities, which matters when your case involves audit, notices, company law or complex income.

q: How much do your services cost?
a: Fees depend on the scope, the volume of transactions and the deadline. We share a clear quote after a short discussion, before any work starts.

q: How does the onboarding process work?
a: You contact us, we understand your requirement, share a document checklist, and begin work after you approve the scope and fee.

q: Is my data safe with you?
a: We use secure channels for document sharing, restrict access to the team handling your file, and keep client information confidential under professional norms.

q: Can I submit documents online?
a: Yes. Scans, photos and PDFs shared securely are enough for most work, and originals are needed only where the law requires.

q: Do you offer monthly compliance packages?
a: Yes. Combined packages for bookkeeping, GST, TDS and payroll are available with a monthly compliance calendar and MIS report.

q: Will I receive acknowledgements and copies of filings?
a: Yes. You receive the filed return or form, its acknowledgement and a record of what was submitted.

q: Which documents do I need to file my income tax return?
a: Typically PAN, Aadhaar, Form 16 or income statements, bank statements, AIS and Form 26AS, investment proofs and details of other income. We share a checklist for your case.

q: Who must file an income tax return?
a: Anyone whose income exceeds the basic exemption limit must file, and certain people must file irrespective of income, such as those with foreign assets or high-value transactions. We confirm your position.

q: What is the last date for filing ITR?
a: It differs by taxpayer category, with later dates for audit cases. We keep you informed of the date applicable to you.

q: Can I file a belated or revised return?
a: Yes, within the time permitted by law. Belated returns may attract a fee and restrict carry-forward of some losses.

q: What is AIS and why does it matter?
a: The Annual Information Statement shows financial transactions reported about you to the department. Reconciling it with your return reduces the chance of mismatch notices.

q: What is the difference between old and new tax regimes?
a: The new regime has lower slab rates with fewer deductions, while the old regime allows many deductions. We compute both and recommend the lower tax.

q: Is capital gains from shares and mutual funds taxable?
a: Yes, and the rate depends on the asset type and holding period. We compute gains and advise on set-off and carry-forward.

q: How is the Income-tax Act, 2025 relevant to my return?
a: The new Act applies from 1 April 2026, while income earned up to 31 March 2026 remains under the Income-tax Act, 1961. We apply the correct law to each year.

q: I received an income tax notice, what should I do?
a: Do not ignore it. Note the due date, then share the notice and related return with us so a reply can be prepared.

q: Who needs GST registration?
a: Businesses crossing the prescribed turnover limit, and certain categories regardless of turnover, such as some interstate and e-commerce suppliers.

q: How often do I file GST returns?
a: Most regular taxpayers file monthly returns, and eligible small taxpayers can opt for quarterly filing under QRMP. Composition dealers file differently.

q: What is input tax credit?
a: It is the credit of GST paid on business purchases, adjusted against GST payable on sales, subject to conditions such as supplier filing and valid documents.

q: What if I do not file GST returns?
a: Late fees and interest apply, and continued default can lead to registration cancellation and notices.

q: Can you cancel or amend my GST registration?
a: Yes. We handle cancellation, revocation and amendments for core and non-core fields.

q: Do I need to file GST if I have no business in a month?
a: Generally yes, as a nil return, unless exempt or cancelled.

q: What is the GST annual return?
a: GSTR-9 is the yearly consolidated return, and GSTR-9C is a reconciliation statement for larger taxpayers.

q: How do I handle a GST notice?
a: Read the notice, check the deadline, and share it with us. We prepare a documented reply and represent you if there is a hearing.

q: Which is better: private limited company, LLP or proprietorship?
a: It depends on funding plans, liability, compliance cost and tax. Proprietorship is simple, LLP is flexible with limited liability, and a private company suits fundraising.

q: How long does company registration take?
a: Typically one to two weeks after documents and name approval.

q: What are the annual compliances of a company?
a: Audit, financial statements and annual return with the Registrar, director KYC, income tax and GST returns, and statutory registers and meetings.

q: What happens if a company misses ROC filing?
a: Additional fees apply per day, and prolonged default can lead to penalties, director disqualification and strike-off.

q: Is director KYC mandatory?
a: Yes, every director with a DIN must complete KYC annually or the DIN gets deactivated.

q: Can I close a company I no longer need?
a: Yes, through strike-off or winding up after clearing filings and liabilities. We advise on the correct route.

q: When is a tax audit required?
a: When turnover or professional receipts cross the prescribed limits or certain presumptive conditions apply. We verify each year.

q: What is the difference between statutory audit and tax audit?
a: Statutory audit arises under company or LLP law, and tax audit under income tax law. Some entities need both.

q: What is TDS and who must deduct it?
a: Tax deducted at source is deducted by the payer on specified payments such as salary, rent, contractor and professional fees, and deposited with the government.

q: Do I need monthly bookkeeping?
a: Regular bookkeeping keeps GST, TDS and tax compliance accurate and gives you monthly MIS reports to run the business.

q: Which accounting software do you work with?
a: We work with popular Indian accounting tools such as Tally and cloud accounting software, and can adapt to what you already use.

q: Can you clean up my past accounts?
a: Yes. We reconstruct and reconcile past books so that returns and statements can be filed properly.
